observation_summary: The FastDateParser incorrectly treated whitespace in date patterns as a regex matching any number of whitespace characters, causing it to successfully parse strings that SimpleDateFormat would reject.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved removing the logic that explicitly handled whitespace by appending '\s*+' to the regex. This was a procedural error in how the parser constructed its internal regex representation for date patterns. Since the fix involved rewriting the logic for processing characters in the pattern string, it falls under Algorithm/Method.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'FastDateParser treats a single white-space as being any number of white-space characters.'
The diff shows the removal of the 'wasWhite' flag and the associated logic that appended '\s*+' to the regex when whitespace was encountered.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix removes a conditional check (if(Character.isWhitespace(c))), the primary issue was the incorrect implementation of the parsing algorithm itself, not a missing guard or validation check.
